description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.

summary.one_liner: REA is an MCP server and CLI that lets AI agents reverse engineer native binaries, JavaScript/Electron apps, .NET assemblies, websites, and other artifacts, returning evidence for each conclusion.
summary.what_it_does: REA connects an AI agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, Android APKs, websites, and many other targets. Native analysis returns pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, and references by using an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, or Kuna installation. Static JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules, imports, routes, IPC, and native add-on relationships without a native engine. The same workflows are available from a terminal through the rea CLI. Many other formats are covered, including Go, Rust, Unity IL2CPP, Godot PCK, GGUF/safetensors, EVM bytecode, SQLite, PE certificates, and packet captures. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. A README section also describes building RL environments from recorded web sessions.
use_cases: reverse engineer a feature in a desktop or Electron app
inspect native binary pseudocode and assembly with an agent
trace JavaScript modules, IPC, and routes in an Electron app
analyze .NET assemblies and Android APKs without source code
recover details from firmware, game binaries, or Go/Rust executables
build an RL environment from a recorded web app session
notable: Single MCP server covering many target types, from native binaries to websites and packet captures
Evidence-backed results that state the limitations behind each conclusion
Static JavaScript/Electron and .NET inspection needs no native analysis engine
Setup command registers the MCP server and workflow instructions with supported agents, with backups of existing config
Builds runnable RL environments from recorded HAR browser sessions
caveats: Native analysis requires a separately installed commercial or third-party engine such as Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, or Kuna; REA grants no tool license
Many targets need extra tools or Linux-specific prerequisites (e.g., procps ps, pwntools, TShark, adb, JADX with a full JDK)
Runtime capture runs or interacts with the target using the user's permissions
keywords: understand how an app feature works
